newsitem.title: POLAND: Cigna to take 49 pct of Polish insurer STU SA. [CORRECTED 14:05 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Cigna to take 49 pct of Polish insurer STU SA. [CORRECTED 14:05 GMT]

text.p: Cigna International, a unit of the U.S. Cigna Corporation, has agreed to take roughly 50-percent stakes in small Polish insurers STU SA and STU Life SA to gain access to Poland, Cigna's European head (corrects from Cigna International's head) said on Tuesday.

"Cigna International has agreed in principle to pursue a joint venture with Polish insurance companies STU and STU LIFE subject to governmental approval by various government agencies in Poland," Gerhard Hornig told a news conference on Tuesday.

Hornig said government approval would likely come in 30 to 60 days and that the entities in their new form, STU Cigna Polska SA and life insurer STU Cigna Zycie SA, could begin operations immediately after.
Hornig said Cigna would reveal the amount to be invested in the firms once government approval came. STU SA had a 0.3 percent market share at the end of 1996.
Private Polish trader Bartimpex and its subsidiary Bank Wschodnio-Europejski SA (BWE) now hold 80 percent of STU SA. STU Life is 35-percent owned by STU SA and 40-percent by BWE.
Bartimpex president Aleksander Gudzowaty said his firm and BWE would remain investors in the two firms.
Cigna International president Kingsley Schubert said Poland accounted for about 19 percent of the estimated $12 billion in insurance premium generated in Central and Eastern Europe.
Schubert told Reuters he saw the Polish general insurance industry growing at 1.5 percent for every one-percent increase of gross domestic product, 2.2 percent for life insurance.
